title: Can a stock Unitree G1 or H1 humanoid carry a stud across a site floor as fast as a labourer?
summary: Single-support inverse dynamics of the Menagerie G1 and H1 carrying a load along a prescribed linear-inverted-pendulum gait (636 cases over payload, step length, step time, ramp and step-up), scored against joint torque limits and the sole. The G1's fastest feasible step is 0.25 m/s unloaded and 0.10 m/s at 4 kg (none at 5 kg); the H1's 0.15 m/s unloaded and 0.07 m/s at 14 kg. A 1:12 ramp leaves the G1's speed unchanged; the H1 finds no step on a ramp. These are pessimistic lower bounds, because the gait has no trunk compensation and the centre of pressure leaves the sole first. A robot holding one piece per trip would have to walk 4–13 m/s to match a labourer carrying three over a 40 m haul, so it loses even at the vendor's quoted ~2 m/s. Preliminary: a prescribed gait and not a policy, falls and energy not scored; the step width, handling times and pieces per trip are my assumptions, swept; nothing is a safety case.
lede: can a stock Unitree G1 or H1 carry a stud as fast as a labourer? A pendulum gait with no trunk compensation gets the G1 to 0.25 m/s unloaded and 0.10 m/s at 4 kg; a robot with one piece per trip would need 4-13 m/s to match a labourer carrying three.
